subject: Post-demo follow-up: vector retrofit & SDK auth plan

Subject: Post-demo follow-up: vector retrofit & SDK auth plan

Hi Amit / Helena,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and solid signal around where Searchly wants to get to. Quick recap from our side and the specific technical questions we promised to follow up on.

Demo recap (high level)
- You currently serve semantic search + a light reranker; looking to replace embeddings provider and centralize retrieval pipeline.
- Key goals: maintain retrieval quality, reduce per-token/embedding cost, and shorten reindex windows.

Outstanding architecture & integration items
1) Vector dimensionality: you mentioned current embeddings are 1536 dims (vendor X). We need to validate mapping options (keep 1536 vs re-embed to 768/512 depending on target model).
2) Batching & throughput: target batch size for your bulk re-index is ~64 and near-real-time updates ~1-4 qps. Need to confirm expected ingest concurrency and latency SLOs.
3) Normalization: you normalize with L2 after dedupe. We should validate whether to preserve that or shift normalization to inference side for stability across models.
4) Migration approach: dual-write vs backfill windows, and a canary strategy for reranker cutover.
5) Auth & SDK: you asked about API key vs OIDC and an SDK quickstart for streaming / structured tool-calls.
6) Routing & fallbacks: how to route requests for low-latency vs cost tiers and automatic fallback to quantized variants.

Action items we propose
- Technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions) to review sample payload and map dims (30–45m).
- Engineering touchpoint to validate bulk reindex throughput and provide an estimate for parallel workers.
- Provide a migration playbook (dual-write + background backfill + canary reranker) and a skeleton SLA with expected ingest cost.

Attachments: I attached your data schema export (searchly_data_schema.csv) and a small sample payload (redwood_sample_payload.json) for Marissa to review. Also attaching a draft SLA sketch (sla-draft-Searchly-v1.pdf).

Can you confirm availability for a technical deep-dive on Thursday or Friday this week? Suggested times: Thu 11/05 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 11/06 09:00–10:00 PT.

Thanks,

--

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: vector retrofit & SDK auth plan

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the summary. Quick answers from our side to help Marissa prep: 

- Dimensions: current embeddings from vendor X are 1536. Our retrieval pipeline (faiss-based) assumes 1536; wed prefer to keep the same dimension if possible to avoid large re-tuning.
- Batch targets: bulk re-index will be around 2M documents, were planning batches of ~64 with a handful of parallel workers (target sustained throughput ~400–800 docs/sec during backfill windows). Real-time updates are light ~1–3 qps.
- Normalization: yes — we currently L2 normalize after dedupe. Stability during cutover is a main concern.
- Reranker: today the reranker is hosted in-house and invoked after retrieval. We are open to moving it to Redwood-managed reranker later but want to keep initial cutover to embeddings only.
- Auth: OIDC would be ideal from a security posture, but we can accept short-lived API keys for initial testing.
- Migration tooling: do you have any utilities to compute embedding diffs or to help map nearest-neighbor drift across dim changes?

If you can include an estimate for cost delta (per-embedding unit comparisons vs current vendor) and an outline of a rollback plan, that'd be helpful. Were available Thu 11/05 10:00 PT for the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Amit

Hi Amit — thanks for the quick context, that helps a lot. I pulled the sample payload you shared and sketched a few practical options below.

Short answers up front
- Keep 1536 if you want minimal retrieval re-tuning; re-embedding to a smaller dim is possible but requires recalibration of FAISS index and reranker.
- For your bulk window (2M docs, batch 64), we recommend chunking the backfill into worker pools of 8–16 parallel actors with batching at the Redwood client layer. We can provide a starter worker template.
- Preserve L2 normalization on the ingest path; additionally, compute and store the pre-normalized vector if you want to evaluate cross-model drift (helps in A/B canaries).

Detailed migration pattern (recommended)
1) Dual-write period (2–7 days): write embeddings to both your current vector store and Redwood-backed embeddings. Run comparison jobs to compute nearest-neighbor overlap (top-K recall) on a holdout set.
2) Backfill in waves: chunk the 2M docs into windows (e.g., 250k docs) to make performance predictable. Use continuous batching + adaptive concurrency to avoid sudden spikes.
3) Canary reranker evaluation: keep current reranker path for the first 5% of traffic; compare metrics (MRR, top1 precision) before moving more traffic.
4) Final cutover: schedule a low-traffic window, validate indexes and rollback plan.

Notes on dimensionality mapping
- If you keep 1536: minimal model drift, low engineering lift.
- If you reduce to 768: better storage + cost, but requires re-indexing and reranker hyperparameter retuning. We can run a small synthetic experiment (50k docs) to estimate delta.

Batching & SDK guidance
- Use Redwood's SDK batching helper (we'll share a snippet) to accumulate requests into size 64 and flush on timeouts — this balances latency and throughput for backfill workers.
- For real-time writes, set a small-batch path (size 1–4) and route to a low-latency instance pool.

Auth & routing
- OIDC + short-lived tokens (recommended) for production. For initial testing, API keys with scoped roles are fine.
- Routing: you can declare policy by latency SLO or cost tier. We'll set up a fallback policy that routes to a quantized variant (lower cost) when higher-capacity pools are saturated.

Migration helpers we can provide
- NN overlap script (top-K recall diffs) — lightweight Python job.
- Sample worker template (Python + Redwood SDK) for parallel backfills.
- Small evaluation harness to compare reranker outputs on a 10k holdout.

Estimated sequencing & timeline
- Technical deep-dive (Thu 11/05) 
- Deliver migration playbook & worker template (by Mon 11/09)
- Run synthetic experiment (50k) and provide delta numbers (by Fri 11/13)

I attached the sample payload you provided (redwood_sample_payload.json) and a draft SLA sketch for budget planning. Sergio — can you take point on an initial cost delta calc and rough quota for the 2M backfill?

Thanks,
